items.title: A logarithmic connection determines meridian eigenvalues from its residue
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional logarithmic connection on a punctured disk, parallel transport through angle θ followed by a commuting endpoint automorphism g has characteristic polynomial equal to that of g exp(iθR), where R is the residue.
items.strategy: Shrink the circle to the singular point, use uniform convergence of the path-ordered ODE to the constant-residue equation, and conjugacy of holonomies along radial paths.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite-dimensional linear ODE and a uniform limit on a compact interval.

items.title: Every rational Cherednik category-O object has finite length
items.statement: For every finite complex reflection group and parameter c, each object of O_c(W,h) has a finite composition series; every simple is the unique simple head of Δ_c(E) for a unique irreducible W-module E.
items.strategy: Use the Euler grading, lowest generalized weights and local h-nilpotence to construct a simple submodule, then bound composition length by the finite sum of bottom-weight dimensions.

items.title: Dunkl operators realize the polynomial standard module
items.statement: The normalized Dunkl operators preserve C[h*], satisfy the rational Cherednik relations there, and identify the polynomial representation with the induced standard module Δ_c(1).

items.title: Finite modules with a connection on a complex polynomial open are vector bundles
items.statement:
Let $R=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n][f^{-1}]$ with $0
e f$, and let $N$ be a finite $R$-module with operators $
abla_i$ satisfying $
abla_i(a v)=(\partial_i a)v+a
abla_i(v)$. At every complex point $p$ with $f(p)
e0$, $N_p$ is free over $R_{\mathfrak m_p}$, and this basis extends to an algebraic open neighborhood of $p$. Thus its coherent sheaf on the complex principal open is an algebraic vector bundle. A finite submodule stable under these operators, and its quotient, have the same property. Integrability is unnecessary for local freeness; if the operators commute, these bundles carry the induced integrable connections. Short exact sequences of such bundles give exact fiber sequences.
items.strategy: Complete local proof in the numbered carrier; see owner construction for exact source and consumer closure.
items.axiom_use: No additional arbitrary choice principle; the costandard Ext argument uses a finite projective Koszul resolution with explicit contraction.

items.title: Dunkl localization gives flat connections on the regular locus
items.statement: For t=1, the Dunkl operators define an injective homomorphism H_{1,c}(W,h) -> D(h_reg)⋊W and an isomorphism after inverting the discriminant. Every localized object of O is finite locally free with an integrable W-equivariant connection, and fiber monodromy is exact.
items.strategy: Use PBW symbols for injectivity, invert the arrangement for surjectivity, and prove local freeness from a finite module with an integrable connection.
items.axiom_use: None; the argument uses filtered algebra, localization, the determinant trick, and elementary differential calculus.

items.title: The KZ monodromy functor and the reflection Hecke algebra
items.statement: Define the reflection braid group from W acting on h_reg, KZ as monodromy of the localized left differential-module connection, and the finite Hecke quotient using positive meridian roots μ_{H,j}=ζ_H^j exp(-2πi r_{H,j}/e_H), where r_{H,j}=Σ_l c_{H,l}(1-ζ_H^{jℓ}).
items.strategy: Fix the action-groupoid, normal-coordinate, endpoint-identification, and horizontal-transport conventions, then define the Hecke quotient without a rank assertion.
items.axiom_use: None; all definitions use the finite reflection arrangement and finite-dimensional linear algebra.

items.title: The standard-module KZ connection has the reflection residue
items.statement: Under the PBW identification Δ_c(E)=C[h*]⊗E, the localized connection is d+Σ_s c_s(dα_s/α_s)(1-s_E). Its logarithmic residue at H is R_H=Σ_{ℓ=1}^{e_H-1} c_{H,ℓ}(1-s_H^ℓ), acting by r_{H,j} on the s_H-character ζ_H^j.
items.strategy: Derive the induced action by the commutator product rule, add the Dunkl correction, and read off the coefficient of dα_H/α_H.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses the induced module, finite sums, and the cyclic stabilizer representation.

items.title: Cherednik category O has a standard-filtered projective generator
items.statement: For every finite complex reflection group and every parameter, rational Cherednik category $\mathcal O_c$ has a finite projective generator which is a direct summand of a generalized standard $G_{n,c}=H_{1,c}\otimes_{S(\mathfrak h)\rtimes\mathbb CW}(\mathbb CW\otimes S(\mathfrak h)/S(\mathfrak h)_{>n})$ for sufficiently large $n$. It is equivalent to finite-dimensional modules over a finite-dimensional algebra. Every indecomposable projective cover $P(E)$ of the simple head $L(E)$ has a standard filtration and an exact sequence $0\to K(E)\to P(E)\to\Delta(E)\to0$, where the standard labels $F$ in $K(E)$ satisfy $a_E-a_F\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$. The standard labels give a finite highest-weight structure for $E<F$ when $a_E-a_F\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$.
items.strategy: Complete local proof in the numbered carrier; see owner construction for exact source and consumer closure.
items.axiom_use: No additional arbitrary choice principle; the costandard Ext argument uses a finite projective Koszul resolution with explicit contraction.

items.title: Hecke relations specialize in the generalized-standard family
items.statement: For every $n\ge0$ the localized generalized standard family $G_{n,c}$ is a finite-rank trivial vector bundle with flat connection whose matrices depend polynomially on the parameter $c$. Its KZ monodromy matrices depend holomorphically on $c$, and for every finite complex reflection group and every parameter the exact defining meridian polynomials of $\mathcal H_{q(c)}(W)$ annihilate $\operatorname{KZ}(G_{n,c})$. Therefore these polynomials annihilate $\operatorname{KZ}(M)$ for every $M\in\mathcal O_c$. This includes all resonant parameters and makes no claim that resonant meridian monodromy is diagonalizable.

items.title: Nilpotent induced Cherednik connections have uniform moderate growth on generic lines
items.statement: For $M\in\mathcal O_c(W,\mathfrak h)$ there is a surjection $U=H_{1,c}\otimes_{S(\mathfrak h)\rtimes W}X\twoheadrightarrow M$ with $X$ a finite-dimensional $S(\mathfrak h)\rtimes W$-module killed by a power of the augmentation ideal of $S(\mathfrak h)$. Under PBW, $U=P\otimes X$. On generic affine coordinate lines its localized connection, and the duals and finite exterior powers of its localized quotients, have horizontal sections of at most power growth at every finite puncture and at infinity on bounded-angle sectors. In fixed rational frames, the exponents and number of punctures are bounded independently of the generic line. Constants and radii may depend on the line. No logarithmic trivialization of the whole induced connection at infinity is asserted.

items.title: Uniformly bounded separate rationality implies rationality
items.statement: Let $U\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ be a nonempty Zariski open subset and let $f$ be a meromorphic function on $U$ (locally a quotient of holomorphic functions). Suppose that there is $D\ge0$ such that on the affine coordinate lines outside a fixed proper algebraic exceptional set in each coordinate direction, whenever its meromorphic restriction is defined, $f$ restricts to a rational function of numerator and denominator degrees at most $D$. Then $f$ is the restriction of an element of $\mathbb C(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ wherever the latter is defined.

items.title: Localized Cherednik monodromy is fully faithful and its image is closed under subquotients
items.statement: Let $\mathcal T=\{M\in\mathcal O_c:M_{\rm reg}=0\}$. Localization identifies $\mathcal O_c/\mathcal T$ fully faithfully with a full subcategory of algebraic $W$-equivariant vector bundles with integrable connection on $\mathfrak h_{\rm reg}$. Monodromy on this subcategory is fully faithful, and its essential image in finite-dimensional $\mathbb C[B_W]$-modules is closed under subobjects and quotients. These assertions hold for every parameter $c$ and finite complex reflection group; they do not assert that every braid-group module comes from $\mathcal O_c$.

items.title: Cherednik costandards have orthogonality and the standard character
items.statement:
Let $D=S(\mathfrak h^*)times\mathbb CW$ and let $E$ be irreducible, with $S(\mathfrak h^*)_{>0}$ acting by zero. The Euler-locally-finite part $
abla_c(E)$ of $\operatorname{Hom}_D(H_{1,c},E)$ lies in $\mathcal O_c$, has simple socle $L(E)$ once, and satisfies $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\Delta(E),
abla(F))=\delta_{EF}\mathbb C$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O}(\Delta(E),
abla(F))=0$. Moreover $[
abla(E)]=[\Delta(E)]$ in $K_0(\mathcal O_c)$, without a real-reflection or self-duality assumption.

items.title: Cherednik BGG reciprocity and the KZ projective rank
items.statement: For every $E,F\in\operatorname{Irr}W$, one has $(P(E):\Delta(F))=[\nabla(F):L(E)]=[\Delta(F):L(E)]$. Put $r_E=\dim\operatorname{KZ}(L(E))$. Then $P_{\operatorname{KZ}}=\bigoplus_E P(E)^{r_E}$ represents the exact vector-space-valued KZ functor and $\dim\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P_{\operatorname{KZ}})=|W|$. This rank calculation uses no dimension or freeness hypothesis on the reflection Hecke algebra; the equality $\dim\mathcal H_{q(c)}(W)=|W|$ remains an explicit extra hypothesis when this is used to prove the quotient equivalence.
items.strategy: Complete local proof in the numbered carrier; see owner construction for exact source and consumer closure.
items.axiom_use: No additional arbitrary choice principle; the costandard Ext argument uses a finite projective Koszul resolution with explicit contraction.

items.title: KZ identifies the torsion quotient with Hecke modules under the Hecke-rank hypothesis
items.statement: If dim_C H_{q(c)}(W)=|W|, then KZ induces O_c(W,h)/O_tor ≃ H_{q(c)}(W)-mod, where O_tor is the kernel of localization to h_reg.
items.strategy: Prove localized monodromy full faithfulness and subquotient closure directly, construct the KZ projective by highest-weight/BGG theory, prove Hecke-map surjectivity, and compare dimensions under the explicit rank hypothesis.
items.axiom_use: None; the explicit rank equality is a hypothesis, not an axiom.

items.title: The trivial reflection group gives the first Weyl algebra
items.statement: For W={1} and dim h=1, H_{1,0} is the first Weyl algebra [y,x]=1 and its polynomial standard module is C[x] with y=d/dx.
items.strategy: Specialize the presentation to the empty reflection set and verify the polynomial action directly.
items.axiom_use: None; the calculation uses the defining presentation and polynomial differentiation.

items.title: Category O is not semisimple at the rank-one parameter c=1/2
items.statement: For W=Z/2 on h=C at c=1/2, the polynomial standard module contains xC[x] and the exact sequence with trivial one-dimensional quotient is nonsplit; hence O is not semisimple.
items.strategy: Compute the Dunkl action on monomials, prove xC[x] is stable, and rule out an invariant complement using multiplication by x.
items.axiom_use: None; the argument uses the rank-one presentation and polynomial algebra.
